body:
Centerbridge Partners LP has acquired technology advisory platform Amplix from lower middle market private equity firm Gemspring Capital Management LLC for roughly $850 million to $875 million.

Norwood, Mass.-based Amplix, formally known as RAB Aggregator LLC, didn’t disclose the financial terms of the deal in its Tuesday, Nov. 17, statement.

The Deal last month reported Centerbridge had prevailed in an auction process that valued Amplix at $800 million to $850 million, or about 17 times Ebitda of $45 million to $55 million, besting rival suitors including KKR & Co. (KKR). Another source subsequently valued the transaction at $875 million.

Centerbridge and Gemspring didn’t immediately return requests for comment on the deal valuation.

Amplix provides technology consulting, procurement, implementation and managed services to more than 3,500 clients nationwide, including BJ’s Wholesale Club Inc., Carnival Corp. (CCL) and sandal maker Reef. The platform advises enterprises across artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, infrastructure, connectivity, customer experience and mobility.

Gemspring formed Amplix in 2022 through the merger of ROI Communications, Blue Front Technology Group and allConnex. Under Gemspring’s ownership, the company completed 15 add-on acquisitions, revamped its go-to-market model, expanded its North American footprint and scaled lifecycle support services across enterprise technology investments.

The Deal identified Amplix as an exit candidate in a May 2025 story following competitive sale processes for sector peers Avant Communications Inc. and Bridgepointe Technologies Inc.

Centerbridge plans to partner with Amplix management to accelerate organic expansion and fund additional M&A as enterprise demand for independent advisory services rises alongside corporate AI adoption.

New York-based Centerbridge makes private equity, private credit and real estate investments, with a focus on flexible, multistrategy approaches across North America and Western Europe. It typically focuses on investments of more than $100 million, often operating within the middle market to large-cap space.

It reportedly raised $3.6 billion for its fifth PE fund in 2024. The PE firm closed its latest opportunistic credit fund, Centerbridge Special Credit Partners V, at $4 billion in September.

Founded in 2015, Westport, Conn.-based Gemspring invests in middle market businesses across the business, consumer, healthcare and industrial services sectors. Gemspring has completed more than 125 acquisitions, typically investing in companies with up to $2 billion in revenue.

Gemspring on Monday announced the closing of its fourth buyout fund, Gemspring Capital Fund IV, at $3.5 billion. It raised $1.7 billion for its third flagship fund in 2023.

Lazard Ltd. was financial adviser and Michael J. Sartor and Daniel W. Vaczy of Kirkland & Ellis LLP provided counsel to Amplix and Gemspring.

Guggenheim Securities LLC was financial adviser to Centerbridge, and Atif I. Azher and Naveed Anwar of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP provided counsel.
